text:
*A. How I approach conflict*
1. I actively look for something in an opposing view that could expand my understanding.
2. I can remain curious about someone’s reasons even when I strongly disagree with their position.
3. I am prepared for my own position on this issue to change.
4. During disagreement, I find myself preparing my response rather than fully listening.
5. Changing my position during a disagreement would feel like losing.
6. A disagreement can be successful if my understanding expands, even when my position stays the same.
*B. How I understand the issue*
7. There are important aspects of this issue that I may not yet see.
8. Addressing this issue involves trade-offs between things that matter.
9. My current position on this issue feels important to who I am.
10. What are the main considerations that shape how you currently see this issue? Where, if anywhere, do they pull in different directions?
*C. How I feel about myself and the future*
11. I feel positive about myself right now.
12. I feel hopeful about people’s ability to work through serious disagreements.
13. I can see a workable way forward on this issue.
*D. How I perceive another panellist*
14. I understand why [name] holds their position on this issue.
15. My impression of [name] goes beyond their position on this issue.
16. I believe [name] wants good outcomes for the people affected by this issue.
17. I consider [name] knowledgeable about this issue.
18. [Name] and I favour similar approaches to addressing this issue.
19. [Name] and I share underlying concerns about this issue.
20. What do you currently think explains [name]’s position on this issue? Say what you are unsure about, too.
*End of the 20-question set.*
